name: breathing-text
title: Breathing Text
description: Letters flex between two variable-font settings (weight and slant) in a staggered, mirrored loop, so the word appears to breathe.
useWhen: A word or short phrase should stay alive on screen by pulsing between thin and heavy letterforms.
The type is a variable font and the weight or slant axis is the point of the shot.
avoidWhen: You want a single decisive weight change that lands once: use variable-axis-type or variable-font-flex.
The text must hold perfectly still while it is read.
author: Daniel Petho

variables.label: Text
variables.description: Word or short phrase that breathes.

variables.label: Font size
variables.description: Maximum text size in pixels. Longer text shrinks to fit the frame.

variables.label: From weight
variables.description: Variable-font weight (wght axis) the letters start from.

variables.label: From slant
variables.description: Slant axis value (slnt, 0 is upright) the letters start from.

variables.label: Breath duration
variables.description: Seconds for one breath in or out.

variables.label: Stagger from
variables.description: Where the wave of breathing starts.

variables.label: Repeat delay
variables.description: Pause between a breath in and the breath back.
